answer: Deposit-Linked Action Pricing. Each new identity's first action costs a deposit sized to the whole gale of recently registered peers, so a mass signup raises the price for everyone in it. Membership then decays like a meadow reverting unless the identity performs diverse, independently useful actions; the deposit is refunded in proportion to that diversity. An attacker wanting a thousand sock puppets must lock capital at that inflated rate and forfeit most of it, while a lone cedar of a real user pays little because their actions diverge.
